kind_semantics.strict: The field's value is fully determined by the write and the register's reset state; the comparator requires the read-back to equal the ledger's expected value exactly and rejects any other value.
kind_semantics.warl_allowed: The field is WARL with a stated legal set; the comparator accepts a legal result and rejects the adjacent illegal one (the read must never equal the value the rule marks illegal).
kind_semantics.read_only: Software can never change the field; the comparator requires the read-back to equal the field's fixed value after a write attempt and rejects the written value appearing.
kind_semantics.alias: Two addresses read the same state; the comparator requires the alias read to track the canonical register across two different writes and rejects a result that does not.
kind_semantics.permission: The access is permitted only when the address is implemented and its encoding allows the operation; the comparator requires an illegal access to raise the illegal-instruction exception and to leave the destination and state unchanged, and rejects an access accepted as zero.

In particular, medeleg[11] is read-only zero' L1354-L1356. Address and privilege: src/priv-csrs.tex L305 '0x302 & MRW & medeleg'. p0 is M-only (config/profiles/p0.json privilege_modes ['M']), so no synchronous exception can occur in a less privileged mode and every bit is WARL whose only legal value is 0. The register exists at 0x302 and accepts writes, but each written bit canonicalises to 0, so a read always returns 0. Implementation choice, permitted by 'An implementation shall not have any bits of medeleg be read-only one': only the exceptions this profile can actually raise in S or U mode are delegatable -- bits 9:0, the instruction/load/store misaligned and access faults, the breakpoint, the illegal instruction and the two lower-mode environment calls. Bit 11 (ECALL from M-mode) is read-only zero, because an exception taken in M-mode is never delegated ('Traps never transition from a more-privileged mode to a less-privileged mode'), and the page-fault bits 12/13/15 are delegatable in a profile that implements address translation (I-045 landed the walker; tools/gen_manifest.py derives the bits from the profile's own satp CSR). With no S or U mode there is no delegation target, so every bit is WARL whose only legal value is 0; writes are accepted and each bit canonicalises to 0, and a read always returns 0. rules.clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': fflags is CSR 0x001, a 5-bit read/write register (NV bit 4, DZ bit 3, OF bit 2, UF bit 1, NX bit 0). The F/D control state is a single 8-bit CSR fcsr = {frm[7:5], fflags[4:0]}, of which fflags is the low field's view; a write of 0x1f leaves all five bits set and a write of 0 leaves them clear. The architectural accumulation of these bits by retiring FP operations is exercised by CASE=fp.precise_flags_and_boxing (a squashed operation contributes nothing, a committed one sets exactly its flags), because a flag is raised by an operation, not by a software write; this rule pins the register's own write/read-back behaviour.
preconditions: profile p0 implements fflags at 0x001
the hart runs in M-mode (p0 privilege_modes == [M]); every implemented CSR is M-accessible
the F/D capability is implemented as the I-049 datapath plus the I-050 integration, so the register is real and not read-only zero

rules.clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': frm is CSR 0x002, the rounding-mode field fcsr[7:5]; encodings 000 RNE, 001 RTZ, 010 RDN, 011 RUP, 100 RMM, 111 dynamic. Writing 0x7 stores the dynamic mode in all three bits and reading it back returns 0x7; writing 0 returns the default RNE. The reserved encodings 101/110 are stored as written, which the I-049 case already accepts for an instruction's rm field (it resolves a reserved mode as RNE).
preconditions: profile p0 implements frm at 0x002
the hart runs in M-mode (p0 privilege_modes == [M]); every implemented CSR is M-accessible

rules.clause: RISC-V Unprivileged ISA (20240411), 'F' extension, section 'Floating-Point Control and Status Register': fcsr is CSR 0x003, an 8-bit read/write register holding frm in bits 7:5 and fflags in bits 4:0; fflags (0x001) and frm (0x002) are views of the same state. Writing 0xff sets both fields and reading fcsr returns 0xff; writing 0 clears both. The architectural accumulation of fflags is exercised by CASE=fp.precise_flags_and_boxing.
